title: Union bound for Johnson–Lindenstrauss distortion
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A\colon\Omega\to\bbr^{k\times d}$ be a measurable random $k\times d$ matrix. Fix a finite set $V\subseteq\bbr^d$ and a parameter $\varepsilon\in\bbr$, and suppose that for every pair $u,v\in V$ the single-vector bad event for the difference $u-v$ has probability at most $2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8)$, that is,
\[
  \mu\bigl\{\,\omega : \varepsilon\,\|u-v\|^2 < \bigl|\,\|A(\omega)(u-v)\|^2 - \|u-v\|^2\,\bigr|\,\bigr\} \le 2\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
Then the probability of the bad-pair event — that some ordered pair $(u,v)\in V\times V$ fails the two-sided distortion bound $(1-\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|A(\omega)(u-v)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2$ — is at most
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: A is a measurable random k×d matrix
V is a finite subset of ℝ^d
